# Commentary on the Top 10 iShares UCITS Equity ETFs by 3-Year Sharpe Ratio

## 1. Fund-by-Fund Notes

**ESIF.L – MSCI Europe Financials Sector (Sharpe 1.942)**
Tracks European banks, insurers and diversified financials. It posted the highest return (37.37%) in the set, but also the highest volatility (19.24%) — the return premium was large enough to more than offset the extra risk, producing the top Sharpe ratio. This is consistent with a rate-driven or re-rating environment being favourable to the financials sector over the period.

**WFNS.AS – MSCI World Financials Sector Advanced (Sharpe 1.929)**
The global counterpart to ESIF, financials sector exposure on a worldwide basis. Lower return (29.32%) than ESIF but also meaningfully lower volatility (15.2%), giving it a Sharpe almost identical to the European sector fund — confirming that financials broadly (not just European banks) delivered strong risk-adjusted results in this window.

**ESPX.AS – S&P 500 Scored and Screened (Sharpe 1.628)**
A US large-cap index modified by ESG/sustainability screens. Return (22.74%) and volatility (13.97%) are both close to plain S&P 500 characteristics, suggesting the screening did not materially distort risk/return versus the broad US market.

**R1VL.L – Russell 1000 Value (Sharpe 1.622)**
US large-cap value exposure. Lowest volatility in the entire top-10 (12.63%), which is the main driver of its ranking, since its return (20.49%) is the lowest in the set.

**CSUS.SW – MSCI USA (Sharpe 1.602)**
Broad-based US equity index, essentially the plain-vanilla large/mid-cap US market. Return and volatility (22.99% / 14.35%) sit close to what a diversified US benchmark would be expected to show, and it has the lowest TER of the group (0.03%).

**SASU.L – MSCI USA Screened (Sharpe 1.577)**
A screened version of the US market. Metrics are close to CSUS.SW, again indicating the screening criteria did not meaningfully alter the risk/return profile relative to the unscreened US index.

**UPAD.L – S&P 500 Paris-Aligned Climate (Sharpe 1.508)**
A climate-tilted variant of the S&P 500 designed to align with decarbonisation pathways. Return (21.59%) and volatility (14.32%) are broadly in line with the standard S&P 500 profile, suggesting the climate tilt has not produced a material Sharpe divergence versus other US large-cap funds in this list.

**CEUU.AS – Core MSCI EMU USD Hedged (Sharpe 1.494)**
Eurozone equities with the currency hedged back to USD. Return (21.26%) and volatility (14.24%) reflect Eurozone-specific market conditions with currency-hedging removing EUR/USD fluctuation as a return driver.

**IUCM.L – S&P 500 Communication Sector (Sharpe 1.479)**
A single-sector US play on communication services. Notably higher volatility (17.44%) than the broad US funds above it, and its return (25.81%) — while higher than most peers — was not enough to compensate for that extra volatility, placing it below the broad-market and financials funds.

**EMID.L – MSCI Europe Mid Cap (Sharpe 1.477)**
European mid-capitalisation equities. Lowest return in absolute terms among sector/style-tilted funds (18.7%), but volatility (12.66%) is also low, keeping the Sharpe ratio competitive despite the modest return.

## 2. Concentration and Bias Observed

- **US equity dominance:** 6 of the 10 funds (ESPX, R1VL, CSUS, SASU, UPAD, IUCM) are directly linked to US large-cap benchmarks (S&P 500 or Russell 1000 variants), meaning the ranking is heavily tilted toward US market performance over the period rather than offering broad geographic diversification.
- **Sector concentration:** Three funds (ESIF, WFNS, IUCM) are single-sector products — two in Financials and one in Communication Services — indicating that sector-specific strategies, particularly Financials, performed strongly on a risk-adjusted basis versus diversified regional or global benchmarks.
- **Financials sector leadership:** The two top-ranked funds by Sharpe are both Financials-sector funds (Europe and World), a clear thematic signal that this sector outperformed on a risk-adjusted basis in the trailing 3-year window covered.
- **Currency/hedging note:** CEUU.AS is a EUR-underlying, USD-hedged product, differentiating its currency exposure from the other funds, which generally carry unhedged USD or EUR exposure depending on the underlying market.
- **Listing venue:** Despite the stated LSE preference, 4 of the 10 funds (WFNS.AS, ESPX.AS, CSUS.SW, CEUU.AS) are not LSE-listed in this dataset, listed instead on Euronext Amsterdam or SIX Swiss Exchange, indicating that for these particular ISINs no LSE line was captured in the screen or none exists.
- **Cost profile:** All 10 funds carry a TER at or below 0.18%, consistent with the sub-0.20% screening threshold, with CSUS.SW as the cheapest (0.03%) and ESIF.L, WFNS.AS and R1VL.L as the most expensive within the group (0.18%).

## 3. Conclusion

This list may be of interest to an analyst or investor who wants to study which broad equity market segments — by sector, style or region — delivered the strongest **historical** risk-adjusted return over the trailing 3-year period, with a specific lens on low-cost, LSE-accessible UCITS structures where available. The pronounced presence of US large-cap and Financials-sector exposure in the top ranks reflects what happened in this specific historical window and should not be read as a structural or permanent characteristic of these market segments.

**This is strictly a historical 3-year risk/return ranking based on trailing Sharpe ratios. It is not a buy recommendation, not an assessment of fund quality or suitability, and not a projection or forecast of future performance.** Past risk-adjusted returns, including the Sharpe ratios shown, offer no guarantee of similar outcomes going forward, and any investment decision would require independent due diligence beyond the scope of this screen.
